chapter_theme: The pure states (நின்மல அவத்தை): when waking, dream and deep sleep subside into turiya and beyond, and grace removes malam, the soul knows itself as the knower, beyond the inert tattvas, and becomes one with Siva. The soul knows only as grace illumines it; one Shakti feeds desire and then withers it; the freed leave heaven and hell behind, and even what is vain, known through grace, is grace.
structure_note: Withdrawal and passing beyond the elements (2304 to 2306); the states, turiya and what survives it (2307 to 2314); the Lord within and self-knowledge given by the guru (2315 to 2331); Shakti and grace in bondage and release (2332 to 2344); the reaching of Siva and those who reach (2345 to 2354). The grouping is mine; many verses are built on a repeated opening word (2312, 2319, 2321, 2330, 2336, 2339, 2340).

2304.reading: Inside a silent well lives a tortoise with five hollows within it; if it withdraws into truth without slipping, it lives a thousand years beyond a tortoise's span.
2304.nuance: ஊமைக் கிணறு (the dumb or silent well) is commonly taken as the body or its inner cavity, and the tortoise drawing in its five as the soul withdrawing the five senses. அழுவைகள் is obscure (hollows, depths). The last line may promise long life to the yogi; the plain and the symbolic readings both stand.

2305.reading: For those who can run past the five above, the elements of air, fire, water and earth with space and the gods Mal, Isan, Brahma and Sadasivan, and mingle beyond them, there is no Death and no thought of their own.
2305.nuance: The gods are traditionally the rulers of the five elements; அங்கி (fire) in line 2 may be a god's name or the element repeated. மேலஞ்சும் ஓடி (running over the five) is taken as passing through the centres of the elements in the body. கருத்தில்லை may mean freedom from the thinking mind or simply 'no concern'.

2306.reading: People do not grasp what the great Veda declares in saying the self became the son; if the self is called Hara's son, then the self as separate is gone and so are the twenty-five.
2306.nuance: The first line seems to echo the Vedic saying that the self is born as one's son. ஐஐந்து (five fives) is taken as the twenty-five tattvas. The argument is compressed and I can't fix whether it affirms or refutes the Vedic claim.

2307.reading: When rising ceases, the three states of waking, dream and deep sleep subside; the conscious soul, held by the Lord in turiya, becomes supremely auspicious and endless at its close.
2307.nuance: சாக்கிரம் (waking), கனவு (dream), சுழுத்தி (deep sleep) and துரியம் (the fourth) are the standard states of the soul. உதயம் அழுங்கில் (when rising is checked) and அந்தி (the close, or twilight) are unclear; பதிதரு சேதனன் may be 'the conscious one given by the Lord' or 'the conscious one who attains the Lord'.

2308.reading: When everything enters into oneself and one becomes all, and one dwells in good turiya, the good soul does not go into the evil thirty-six but becomes awareness and reaches Siva's state, from which there is no going.
2308.nuance: ஆறாறு is the thirty-six tattvas, called பொல்லாத (evil) as what binds. செல்லாச் சிவகதி may be 'the Siva-state not reached by going' or 'from which one does not leave'.

2309.reading: As heated iron, even after the fire is taken away, keeps a heat like fire, so in turiya, where the instruments have died away, the stain of karma steeped in does not leave.
2309.nuance: வாதனை (vasana) is the impression a deed leaves behind. The verse warns that reaching turiya does not by itself remove karma's residue; I read it as a check on the confidence of 2308.

2310.reading: Nandi, whose form is the Veda and the rest, came and gave grace in the clear waking state; when the states as they came are closed and let go, that state beyond delusion is the Supreme.
2310.nuance: தெரிநனா அவத்தை (the clear or discerning waking state) is taken as the waking state of the freed soul. ஆன மாலதீதம் is obscure: மால் அதீதம் (beyond delusion) or a form of மலாதீதம் (beyond malam).

2311.reading: If the pure state beyond touches the embodied state, the Father's grace does not leave; there, being oneself, practising a samadhi that does not touch the mind's pleasure, grace becomes the first step to being one with the Father.
2311.nuance: சுத்த அதீதம் (the pure beyond) and சகலம் (the soul's embodied state) are technical terms. சித்த சுகம் is taken as the pleasure of the mind, which this samadhi does not seek.

2312.reading: He divided the whole of the body into two halves, set me apart and sent me everywhere; then, leaving me in kevala with a grace that does not divide, the Father who makes no division came and stayed joined with me.
2312.nuance: வேறுசெய் opens every line: twice the Lord separates, twice he does not. இரு பாதியின் மெய்த்தொகை may be the body's two halves or the two kinds of bond. கேவலம் is the soul's isolated state, bound only by anava.

2313.reading: Like a whirling leaf-wheel, a firebrand swung in a circle, waves on the sea or a churning stick in curds, the soul stays in its malam and is turned through heaven, hell and earth according to its deeds; by grace it is freed of these.
2313.nuance: All four images are of endless turning in one place. அறங்காண் (seen by deeds) and கிரங்கா (perhaps 'not grieving' or 'unsteady') are unclear, so who is freed and how exactly is not fixed.

2314.reading: When the state of oneself becoming Siva is reached, malam, the kinds of bond, the gunas and the soul's limiting adjuncts fade like the moon before the sun.
2314.nuance: உபாதி is the limiting adjunct. The last word பலராவே is unclear; the sun and moon image needs a sense like 'grow faint', and I take it so.

2315.reading: Fire, water and air are there; the sun and the moon dwell there; worthy Mal, four-faced Brahma and Rudra's light are all within the heart.
2315.nuance: Plainly, the elements, the lights and the gods are within. Tradition also reads the sun and moon as the right and left breath channels and the gods as rulers of centres in the body; that reading is symbolic and not fixed by the verse.

2316.reading: For one who tames the five elephants, lights the wick of knowledge, enters it and looks at the flesh until its darkness is gone, the way to climb to the sky is easy.
2316.nuance: The five elephants are the senses. The flesh (ஊன்) is not despised but looked into until it is lit. வானகம் may be heaven, release, or the space at the crown of the head of yogic practice.

2317.reading: The breath that sways the dancing foot, the sound of the damaru rising as it is struck, and the Vedas and Agamas rising in song: this is how I saw them within the nadi.
2317.nuance: Siva's dance with its drum and the scriptures it sounds are placed within the body's channel. Whether this is a vision in practice or an image for the dance in the body is not fixed.

2318.reading: The ancient austerity done in an earlier understanding can be known once the later understanding is gained; knowing oneself is knowledge, and anything else known afterwards is a ghoul's knowledge.
2318.nuance: முன்னை அறிவு and பின்னை அறிவு play on earlier and later knowing; one reading is that tapas of past lives bears fruit as present insight. பேயறிவு (a ghoul's knowledge) is blunt contempt for knowing that leaves out the self.

2319.reading: Being without action is Siva's bliss; those who rest without action do not seek Siva-yoga, do not mingle with the world, and only they have the work done.
2319.nuance: செயலற்றிருத்தல் is traditionally taken as giving up one's own agency to the Lord, not idleness. செய்தியுண்டாம் is open: 'there is achievement' or 'there are tidings'. Even seeking Siva-yoga is counted as action.

2320.reading: If the samadhi in which oneself becomes Him is reached, malam is cut off and that bound-soul nature goes; for those who remove the eight defects and become one, the flawless body stays on the great earth.
2320.nuance: The body staying on earth after malam is cut is read as release while living (jivanmukti). ஊனங்கள் எட்டு (eight defects) are not named; they may be the eightfold subtle body or eight bonds.

2321.reading: Hara's unfailing feet and his Shakti, unfailing darkness and light, the soul that appears, and unfailing action and knowledge meet from of old, and the soul is steeped between unfailing bondage and release.
2321.nuance: தொலையா (unfailing, unending) opens every line. அணு (the atom) is the Siddhanta name for the soul; பெத்தம் is bondage. The grammar is loose and the reading is a guess at the joints.

2322.reading: Through the Shakti who encompasses bondage and release as they arise, the soul is now bewildered and now clear; the knowledge she gives becomes the means to her, and a light to the unsupported light within.
2322.nuance: மான்றும் தெருண்டும் (bewildered and cleared) is the soul's state in bondage and in release, both under the same Shakti. ஊன்றல் இல்லா உள்ளொளி may be the soul's own light, which has no footing of its own.

2323.reading: The thirty-five and the one do not know, and I did not know myself, the one who knows; Nandi graced me, saying 'You are the one who knows', and I came to know that I am the knower.
2323.nuance: ஐஏழும் ஒன்றும் (five sevens and one) is taken as the thirty-six tattvas, which in Siddhanta are inert. The guru does not give the soul knowledge but shows it that it is the knower.

2324.reading: What was seen within the flesh: the lord of the knowledge in which oneself becomes Him, first of the gods, the light of a great gem, and the flawless Shakti of sweet grace in faultless knowledge.
2324.nuance: The verse is a list of objects with one verb at the end, கண்டதே (it was seen). Siva and Shakti are both seen within the flesh (ஊனிடை).

2325.reading: Light and darkness and Parai, and what is called tender regard within Parai, are apart from the soul; passing beyond tenderness, grace and clarity, the grace that makes clear is Siva's bliss.
2325.nuance: பரை is the supreme Shakti; அளி (tender regard), அருள் and தெருள் are close words, and the distinctions between them are not explained. The verse seems to rank stages of grace below a final one.

2326.reading: In Hara's grace-Shakti, which is bliss, the soul that has come to its end does samadhi itself; if the flesh ends and one feels within as awareness, the Lord's end is reached: this is the great saying.
2326.nuance: The verse plays on அந்தம் (end): ஆனந்தம், தான் அந்தம், ஊன் அந்தம், கோன் அந்தம். மகாவாக்கியம் (the great saying) is the Vedantic term for the identity statements, here given a Saiva sense; which saying is meant is not stated.

2327.reading: There is no need to teach those who are sunk without knowledge, nor those who are full of knowledge; the wise who know teach only those who, having gained knowledge, stand in unknowing.
2327.nuance: The third group is the fit disciple. அறிவுற்று அறியாமை எய்தி may mean those who have learned enough to know they do not know, or those who have passed through knowledge into a higher unknowing.

2328.reading: Sat, asat and sadasat come together; the conscious and the inert stand as Siva's consciousness; in turiya, where pure and impure do not begin, the pure with the three are beyond words.
2328.nuance: In Siddhanta சத்து (the real) is the Lord, அசத்து the bond and சதசத்து the soul, which takes the nature of what it joins. மூன்றுடன் (with the three) may be these three or three states.

2329.reading: The soul does not know by itself, yet it is not without knowing; it knows, and its knowing is sadasat; so when both stand as Hara's grace, it knows of itself and abides with Siva.
2329.nuance: This is the Siddhanta account of the soul as சதசத்து: it can know, but only when something illumines it. The verse places that illumining in grace.

2330.reading: Only for those who have reached tattva-knowledge does tattva-knowledge stand reached; in tattva-knowledge, as oneself becomes Him, the bliss of tattva-knowledge begins.
2330.nuance: தத்துவ ஞானம் opens every line. It may mean knowledge of the tattvas or knowledge of the real; the verse moves from attaining it to its bliss.

2331.reading: When one knows oneself and becomes oneself with Siva, the abiding malam and gunas die and birth ends; then follows true release, the great light of sanmarga, and the good seal of knowledge is reached.
2331.nuance: சன்முத்தி is taken as true release. ஞானத்து முத்திரை may be a literal hand-seal of the jnani or the sealing of knowledge.

2332.reading: Knowledge is his body, action his middle limbs and the will that reaches him his life; since the Supreme takes this form and is the seed of the five acts, the silent ones obtained the seal of knowledge.
2332.nuance: Jnana, kriya and iccha (knowledge, action, will) are the Lord's three Shaktis; here they are his body, limbs and life. மோனிகள் are the silent sages.

2333.reading: Knowledge is the soul's truth, will its measure, action the soul's, and maya the subtle for the soul; he who feeds these to the soul is the feeder, and he is within that mind, not within the soul's word.
2333.nuance: மானம் (measure) and சூக்கம் (the subtle) are unclear here. The plain point is that the Lord gives the soul its powers and is within it beyond what the soul can say.

2334.reading: The action, will and knowledge of the ancient Siva and of the souls arise from undying Mahamaya and maya; leaving the void of flawless cause and effect, Siva is beyond the undying Santa.
2334.nuance: சாந்தாதீதன் (beyond Santa) names Siva above the highest kala, சாந்தி. That Siva's own powers should come from maya is surprising, and the line may mean only that their workings appear through maya.

2335.reading: The Lord becomes all, what is not and what is, yet is neither not-being nor being; whatever one says of him, he is far beyond far; but understood quickly, he becomes the life of life.
2335.nuance: The verse turns on the gap between saying and understanding: in speech the Lord is ever farther, in understanding the nearest.

2336.reading: Shakti feeds the soul's desire and wanders with it; knowledge withers the soul's desire and ends it; because she feeds it and stays with it, by withering the soul's desire she brings it to the high state.
2336.nuance: உயிரிச்சை (the soul's desire) opens every line. The same Shakti first feeds desire and then withers it; tradition reads this as concealment followed by grace.

2337.reading: Those freed of the five malams become Siva and join him; those not at one remain in the darkness of the five malams, of the kind that go from earth to heaven and hell; no one sees that these too are grace.
2337.nuance: ஐம்மலம் (five malams) is traditionally anava, karma, maya, mayeya and tirodhayi. The last line is taken to say that heaven and hell are themselves grace, a ripening, but the grammar is unsure.

2338.reading: What those who have reached do through the great maya-Shakti, through the great Shakti of knowledge and through the great Shakti of the world: all of it is the Lord's grace.
2338.nuance: இருமாயா may be 'great maya' or 'the two mayas', pure and impure. எய்தினர் (those who have reached) are the freed, whose acts are counted as the Lord's.

2339.reading: The reformed have left wretched hell, left splendid heaven, left the gathering of crowded flowers, and, becoming Siva, left what is vain.
2339.nuance: திருந்தினர் (those set right) opens every line. செறிமலர் கூட்டம் is obscure: the pleasures of the senses, the company of women adorned with flowers, or the world of births. அவம் (the vain) answers சிவம் in sound.

2340.reading: Those who do not know the vain and Siva do not know; those who know the vain and Siva know; if they know the vain and Siva through grace, both the vain and Siva become his grace.
2340.nuance: அவமும் சிவமும் opens every line, pairing the futile with the auspicious. The final claim is that even what is vain, known through grace, is his grace.

2341.reading: Grace-Shakti is like heat in fire; with the substance being He, it joins awareness; darkness turned to light returns as the three malams; the holy grace, the blissful one, is the true substance.
2341.nuance: Heat in fire is the classic image for Shakti inseparable from Siva. Line 3 is unclear: perhaps light can fall back into the three malams, or grace works even through them.

2342.reading: When the sun rises, the lotus and the rest differ in what they do by their deeds; the sun with its rays sets them moving; that it divides without dividing is the distinction of grace.
2342.nuance: One sun opens some flowers and closes others; tradition reads this as one grace working differently on souls by their karma. பதுமாதிகள் is taken as 'lotuses and others'.

2343.reading: Difference, non-difference and shifting difference-in-non-difference, awareness and joined awareness, awareness and nada, and nada with naga-nada and the nadas that follow: all are the will of the Lord's grace.
2343.nuance: பேதம், அபேதம், பேதாபேதம் are the three ways of relating soul and Lord argued among the schools. நாகநாதம் and the other nadas are technical and I can't fix them. ஆதன் may be the Lord or the soul.

2344.reading: Like the deed that makes a false puppet dance, he makes the elements he spread dance, creating and the rest; through the gathering of earthly things he brings awareness and settles the soul: that is Hara's grace.
2344.nuance: பொய்க்கரி may be a puppet elephant or a false image moved by strings. பூவியல் கூட்டம் is taken as the assembly of earthly things.

2345.reading: He who knew himself, going off without stopping, becoming the end, reaching in himself all that is and is not, separate and entering space, gained release; that confusion reaching a clarity not yet clear, at the touch becomes Siva.
2345.nuance: The grammar is very loose. அம்மருள் தேறாத் தெளிவுற்று (that confusion gaining a clarity not reached by reasoning) is a guess.

2346.reading: Turning again to love of the rare holy feet that are worthy to touch, going by grace along the ordained way, spurring and mounting the great horse of Siva-knowledge and leaping across, one can reach Siva.
2346.nuance: மா here is taken as horse, so Siva-knowledge is a mount one rides across. விதிவழி (the ordained way) may be scriptural rule or the course set by grace.

2347.reading: Those who have reached him are the charanas, the siddhas and those in samadhi; those who achieve true knowledge of the tattvas; the blissful in whom love comes first; and those whose nature is pure grace.
2347.nuance: சாரணர் are heavenly wanderers, சித்தர் the perfected. சத்த அருள் may be 'pure grace' (சுத்த) or 'the grace of sound'.

2348.reading: The tattvas speak of two, oneself and He; in the state where self and He are not two, those in kevala do not think 'I'; to become oneself without a self is the purity of the tattva.
2348.nuance: தான் and அவன் open three lines. கேவலத்தானவர் may be those in the soul's isolated state, who cannot think at all, or those in a pure solitude; the verse seems to set duality, non-duality and a selfless self in order.

2349.reading: The chief who knows himself within himself sets out to know his Lord within himself; if he does not rest in himself, his Lord within him is hard to reach as well.
2349.nuance: தன் ஐ (his master) is taken as the Lord, or the guru; ஐ also suggests the five senses, but 'lord' fits better. Self-knowledge is the way to the Lord, not a rival to him.

2350.reading: Do not cry 'I cannot know'; once you have gone the way of the path and met him face to face, he who can work as the two lights comes as one light within my heart.
2350.nuance: இருசுடர் (two lights) is traditionally the sun and moon, and in yoga the two breaths. The shift from 'you' to 'my heart' is the poet speaking from his own case.

2351.reading: One clay becomes many fine vessels, and in all the wombs one thinks of there is one; one eye sees many things but does not see itself; the Lord stands in just that way.
2351.nuance: Two images: the clay present in all its pots, and the eye that sees all but itself. ஒருவனே may be the Lord in all wombs or the one soul passing through them.

2352.reading: He guards the seven worlds from within; some close up and speak of him through qualities; those who do not think of Siva waste away; those who do not close up can come and receive him.
2352.nuance: கூம்பு is to close like a flower, or to fold the hands in worship. Whether closing is narrowing the mind or worshipping is unclear, and the verse's contrast depends on it.

2353.reading: Those who do not know the mark cannot see the mark; for those who do not know it, union is a great matter; unite in a way the mark is not known, and having united, stay without knowing knowledge, and you become the swan too.
2353.nuance: குறி (mark, sign, target) is unexplained; it may be the object of meditation or the Lord's form. அன்னம் may be the swan (hamsa, the breath or the freed soul) or food. கூடல் may be union or yogic joining.

2354.reading: Is it the flesh or the life that has the joy? While the Lady of the gods stands bewildering them, people who say 'we know, it is we who are great' do not know birth and death themselves.
2354.nuance: வானோர் தலைவி (Lady of the gods) is taken as Shakti in her veiling work, or as maya. The question in line 1 is left for the reader.

links.note: Both use the tortoise drawing in its five. The Kural makes restraint of the senses in one birth a shelter through seven; Tirumular puts the tortoise in a silent well and promises it a thousand years if it withdraws into truth.

Both treat the five senses as elephants to be mastered (in the Kural through the goad of firmness, as Parimelazhagar reads it). The Kural's reward is the field of release; Tirumular adds a lamp of knowledge lit inside the body.
The Kural defines understanding as seeing the true thing in whatever thing appears; Tirumular narrows it to knowing oneself, and calls every other knowing a ghoul's.
251 says those who know themselves bow to the Lord and find him kin; 2318 says such self-knowing is the only knowledge that counts.
2323 has Nandi tell the soul it is the knower; 2329 adds that the soul does not know by itself and knows only when grace illumines it.
Both use fire and its heat. In 2309 the heat left in iron after the fire is gone is karma's residue; in 2341 heat inseparable from fire is grace inseparable from the Lord.

417 makes the Lord the potter who shapes pots and births; 2351 likens him instead to the one clay in all vessels, and to the eye that sees all but itself. The two images give maker and inner presence.

2305 says that for those who can run past the five elements and their gods, காலனும் இல்லை, there is no Death. Kural 269 says those who have gained the power of austerity can even leap past Death (கூற்றம் குதித்தலும் கைகூடும்). Both make Death something a disciplined person passes beyond; the Kural names the means as tapas, the Tirumanthiram as passing through the elements.

2307 places the soul's fulfilment in turiya: held by the Lord there (பற்றாம் துரியத்து) it becomes supremely auspicious. Thiruppugazh 1049 says the abode of supreme wisdom is not reached even above turiya (துரிய மீது சாராது). The conflict holds on the reading that 2307's turiya is the goal itself; if 2307 describes only a stage, as later verses of the chapter suggest, the two agree.

2308 says that dwelling in turiya the soul does not go into the evil thirty-six (பொல்லாத ஆறாறு) and reaches Siva's state. Thiruppugazh 203 also seeks a light beyond the thirty-six (ஆறாறின் அதிகம்) but places it beyond turiya (பர துரியாதீதம்), past what yogis reach. The song keeps the Tirumanthiram's terms and moves the goal one step further.

2309 says that in turiya, even with the instruments gone, the stain of karma stays, like heat in iron taken from the fire. 2279 says birth does not end merely by knowing oneself in turiya (தன்னை அறிந்தும் பிறவி தணவாதால்). Both verses, in the chapters on the states, refuse to make turiya by itself the end of bondage.

Both use iron changed by a process. In 2309 iron taken from the fire keeps its heat (வாய்ந்த கனலென வாதனை), so the old state lingers; in 2051 iron turned to gold never becomes iron again (மறித்து இரும்பாகா), so the new state is final. Together they set karma's residue against the guru's grace as two kinds of lasting change.

2309 warns that in turiya, where the instruments have died (கரணம் இறந்த), karma's stain stays. Thiruppugazh 1055 asks for a state beyond turiya (துரிய மேற்படு) that has left the instruments (கருவி கரண நீத்த), and implies that Kama's arrows cannot strike there. Read together, the song places beyond turiya the immunity that 2309 denies to turiya itself.

Thiruppugazh 1218 asks the Lord to separate Pati, pasu and pasam each from each without stain (வேறு வேறு செய்தருள்வாயே) so the poet may find the way. 2312 uses the same verb four times: the Lord separates (வேறுசெய்தான்) and then, with a grace that does not separate (வேறுசெய்யா அருள்), stays joined with the soul. The verse carries the song's plea one step on: discrimination is followed by union.

2313 pictures the soul in its malam turning endlessly like waves on the sea (கடலில் திரை) through heaven, hell and earth, freed only by grace. Kural 10 says only those who reach the Lord's feet swim the great sea of births. Both make release from the round of births depend on the Lord, and both use the sea for it.

2314 says that when the soul becomes Siva, malam, bonds and gunas fade like the moon before the sun. Naladiyar 51 says sin cannot stand before austerity as darkness dies when a lamp comes in, but darkness rushes back when the oil runs out. The Naladiyar's lamp limits the victory to the life of the merit that feeds it; the Tirumanthiram's sun is the Siva-state itself and has no oil to run out.

2315 says fire, water, air, sun, moon, Mal, Brahma and Rudra's light are all within the heart (உள்ளத்துளாரே). 1823 makes the heart the great temple (உள்ளம் பெருங்கோயில்) and the body the shrine. 2315 places the cosmos and its gods in the heart; 1823 turns the same inner space into a place of worship.

2316 tells the one who tames the five senses to light the wick of knowledge (ஞானத் திரி) and look into the flesh until its darkness goes. 2367 sets the lamps of maya and of the body, which go out or smoulder, against the pure lamp and a distant lamp the speaker seeks. Both put the body's light against knowledge's light; 2367 adds that even the pure lamp is not the end of the search.

2318 says the ancient austerity of former understanding (முன்னை அறிவு) is known when later understanding (பின்னை அறிவு) comes, and that knowing oneself is knowledge. 2288 uses the same pair: knowing oneself through the truth of austerity known afterwards, and coming to joy when former knowledge ends. The two are close variants in different chapters, and 2288 names the Lord found by that self-knowing.

2319 says that being without action (செயலற்றிருக்க) is Siva's bliss, and that those who rest so do not even seek Siva-yoga. 2635 calls simply staying still (சும்மா இருந்திடம்), maya left and the self hidden, the test. Both make the end a stillness beyond effort, even spiritual effort.

1678 defines the Siva garb as those who, free of delusion and desire, rest without action (செயலற்றிருப்பார் சிவவேடத்தாரே). 2319 uses the same phrase four times and calls that rest Siva's bliss. The Siva-garb chapter makes it the mark of the true ascetic; 2319 makes it the state itself.

724 says the body must be kept because without it true knowledge cannot be firmly gained (உடம்பை வளர்த்தேன் உயிர் வளர்த்தேனே). 2320 says that after the samadhi in which one becomes Him, malam is cut and the flawless body (ஈனமில் காயம்) stays on earth. 724 keeps the body for the sake of knowledge; 2320 shows the body that remains once that knowledge is reached.

2322 says that under the one Shakti who surrounds bondage and release the soul is now bewildered and now clear (மான்றும் தெருண்டும்). 2336 says Shakti first feeds the soul's desire and then withers it (ஊட்டி ... வாட்டி) to bring it to the high state. Both give one power both the binding and the freeing.

In 2323 Nandi tells the speaker 'you are the one who knows' (அறிகின்றாய் நீ), and he comes to know himself as the knower. In 2357 Nandi teaches him that knowledge is his form (அறிவு வடிவு), and he remains as that form. The two are close variants: the guru does not add knowledge but shows the soul its own nature as knowing.

2324 ends a list of Siva and Shakti with one verb: they were seen within the flesh (ஊனிடைக் கண்டதே). 1823 calls the body of flesh the Lord's shrine (ஊனுடம்பு ஆலயம்). Both place the Lord in the flesh, which is honoured, not despised.

2326 says that when the soul ends in Hara's grace and feels itself as awareness, the Lord's end is reached, and calls this the great saying (மகாவாக்கியம்) without naming it. 2402 names it: knowing soul and Siva is 'thou art that' (தொந்தத்தசி), and action ceasing, the soul becomes knowledge and subsides. 2402 supplies the saying 2326 points to and reads it as both Vedanta and Siddhanta.

2327 says there is no need to teach those already full of knowledge (அறிவிற் செறிவோர்); the wise teach only those who have learned and stand in unknowing. Kural 718 says speaking before those who understand (உணர்வது உடையார்) is like watering a crop that is already growing. On Parimelazhagar's reading, that such speech makes the growth greater, the two disagree on whether the knowing are worth addressing; on the plain reading that the watering is redundant, they agree.

2328 joins sat, asat and sadasat, sets the conscious and inert in Siva's consciousness (சித்தும் அசித்தும் சிவசித்ததாய்), and names a state where pure and impure do not begin. 2058 uses the same three and the same pairs: the guru shows sat, asat and sadasat, sets சித்தும் அசித்தும் in Siva, and speaks a word beyond சுத்தம் அசுத்தம். The two are a near-repeat; 2058 makes the doctrine the guru's teaching, 2328 the state of the pure.

2330 says that in tattva-knowledge (தத்துவ ஞானம்), as the self becomes Him, its bliss begins. 2611 says the knowers of tattva who know themselves (தத்துவ ஞானிகள்) untie former karma and crush later karma by Siva's grace. 2611 shows what that knowledge does to karma; 2330 what it becomes.

2331: knowing oneself and becoming one with Siva, malam and the gunas die and birth ends (பிறப்பறும்). 2369: removing the great malam, knowing oneself and abiding in the ancient Lord, birth does not come again (வாரா பிறப்பே). The same sequence of self-knowledge, loss of malam and end of birth closes two neighbouring chapters.

2332 says the silent sages (மோனிகள்) obtained the seal of knowledge (ஞானத்து முத்திரை). Thiruppugazh 1112 asks to attain the silence that is the seal (முத்திரையா மோனம்), beyond the thirty-six tattvas and the instruments. The song uses the Tirumanthiram's pairing of silence and seal as the goal of its plea.

1540 calls Nandi far and near (சேயன் அணியன்), pure to those who can look without wavering. 2335 explains the pair: whatever one says of the Lord he is far beyond far (தூராகி தூரம்), but understood quickly he is the life of life. 2335 makes speech the cause of the distance and understanding the cause of the nearness.

Kural 370 says that giving up craving, never satisfied, at once gives a nature that never shifts (ஆரா இயற்கை அவாநீப்பின் ... பேரா இயற்கை தரும்). 2336 says the soul's desire is withered by knowledge and so reaches the high state, but adds that the same Shakti first fed that desire (உயிரிச்சை யூட்டி). The Kural states the result; the Tirumanthiram makes both the craving and its ending the work of one power.

2337 ends: no one sees that heaven, hell and earth, through which the bound go, are grace (அவையருள்). 2544 says the Lord set hell, heaven and endless births for souls by grace (உயிர்க்கு அருளால் வைத்தான்) to make the unclear mind clear. Both make even hell part of grace; 2544 says what it is for.

2319 says that those who rest without action are the ones who have the work done (செய்தியுண்டாமே). 2338 says that whatever those who have reached do, through the Shaktis of maya, knowledge and the world, is the Lord's grace (இறையருள் தானே). 2338 explains the paradox of 2319: the freed act, but the acts are not theirs.

2339 says the reformed leave hell, leave splendid heaven too (திருவார் சுவர்க்கம்), and become Siva. Kural 346 says one who cuts off 'I' and 'mine' enters a world higher than the gods' (வானோர்க்கு உயர்ந்த உலகம்). Both place the goal above heaven; the Tirumanthiram says outright that heaven must be left.

2337 says no one sees that heaven, hell and the darkness of malam are grace. 2340 says that when the vain and Siva (அவமும் சிவமும்) are known through grace, both become his grace. 2340 states as a rule of knowing what 2337 states of the soul's journeys: what is seen through grace is grace.

2342 says one sun opens some flowers and not others according to their deeds, so grace divides without dividing (பேதித்தப் பேதியா). 248 says one rain feeds sweet trees and the bitter kanjirai alike. The same pattern of one undivided giver and many different receivers appears for grace and for rain; 2342 puts the difference in the receivers' karma.

Thiruppugazh 207 has the poet dance like a string-puppet (பாவை ... கயிறுவிதம்) driven by his two deeds, a picture of misery. 2344 uses the false puppet made to dance by the deed (பொய்க்கரி யாட்டும் வினை) for the Lord moving the elements, and calls it Hara's grace that settles the soul. The same image is a complaint in the song and a theology of grace in the verse.

564 speaks of a horse the lord of the five rides to salvation, traditionally the breath, which throws the false. 2346 makes the horse Siva-knowledge (சிவஞான மா), mounted and spurred to leap across to Siva. The same mount carries the soul in both, breath in the yoga chapter and knowledge here.

2347 lists siddhas and those in samadhi (சித்தர் சமாதியர்) among those who have reached the Lord. Thiruppugazh 1016 lists the nine siddhas in their caves (குகையில் நவநாதர்) first among those who do not know him. The conflict holds if the siddhas are the same class in both; the song may mean siddhas who rely on their powers, which 2347 does not praise.

2279 says birth does not end merely by knowing oneself (தன்னை அறிந்தும் பிறவி தணவாது); the pervading Stainless must be known. 2349 says the one who knows himself within himself sets out to know his Lord within, and without resting in himself the Lord is hard to reach. Together they make self-knowledge necessary but not sufficient.

704 speaks of the yogi who sees at the juncture how the moon meets the sun. 2350 says that the one who works as two lights (இருசுடர்) comes as one light within the heart. Both join the two lights; 704 as a yogic seeing, 2350 as the Lord's coming to one who said 'I cannot know'.

1540 says people bewildered by the deceiver (மாயன் மயக்கிய மானுடர்) do not know what the body is for. 2354 says that while the Lady of the gods holds them bewildered (மயக்கத்து உறநிற்க), people who think they know do not know their own birth and death. Both trace this ignorance of the body and its life to a divine bewildering.

source_issues: 2310 line 4: ஆன மாலதீதம் is obscure; possibly a form of மலாதீதம் (beyond malam).
2314 line 4: பலராவே does not give the expected sense (fade) and may be corrupt.
2347 line 3: தலைப்ட்ட is a misprint for தலைப்பட்ட.
2353 line 2: குறிஅறி யார்கடம் may be divided wrongly (யார்கள் தம் or யார் கடம்).
2335 line 2: இல்லதம் is likely a misprint for இல்லதும்.
